strategies.summary: Wrap the entire forward pass (or at minimum the blocks sequential + head) with torch.compile using mode='reduce-overhead' and fullgraph=True. This captures the full MBConv stack as a single compiled graph, eliminates Python dispatch overhead for the 13-block sequential, and allows the compiler to fuse BN+ReLU and adjacent elementwise ops automatically through inductor.
implementation_hints: In init_body, after building self.blocks, wrap it: self.blocks = torch.compile(self.blocks, mode='reduce-overhead', fullgraph=True).
Alternatively, compile the entire model's forward by overriding __call__ or by compiling ModelNew as a whole in a factory function in user_helpers.
Use torch.compile(model, mode='reduce-overhead') in user_helpers and return the compiled model; this avoids modifying init_body directly.
Set dynamic=False since the input shape (10, 3, 224, 224) is fixed in the benchmark, allowing static shape specialization.
CUDA graphs are implicitly used by reduce-overhead mode for fixed shapes, which can eliminate most kernel launch latency across the 13 MBConv blocks.
If fullgraph=True causes graph breaks on the MBConv residual add, fall back to fullgraph=False to allow partial compilation.
strategies.expected_gain: Moderate to high: the 13-block MBConv sequential has significant Python dispatch overhead. reduce-overhead mode with CUDA graphs can cut per-forward overhead substantially for fixed-batch inference. Most gains come from kernel launch coalescing rather than compute.
risk_notes: torch.compile warm-up takes several seconds on first call; the benchmark must be using a warmed-up timing loop for this to help.
fullgraph=True may fail if any MBConv uses Python control flow (e.g., stride-conditional skip connections); check the MBConv definition.
reduce-overhead mode uses CUDA graphs which require fixed tensor addresses; incompatible with dynamic memory allocation inside blocks.
This approach does not require any cuda_cu/cuda_cpp changes, making it low-risk for compile errors.
If the benchmark runner calls model() in a loop, the CUDA graph replay benefit is real; if each call is isolated, warm-up cost may dominate.
forbidden_patterns: Do not use torch.compile in training mode without disabling cudnn benchmarking
Do not set dynamic=True â the input shape is static

review_notes.openai-compatible: Potentially useful in a general PyTorch setting, but less aligned with the search constraints emphasizing CUDA kernel edits around normalization anchors. Warm-up cost, graph-break risk, and benchmark sensitivity reduce confidence, and gains may overlap poorly with existing cuDNN-optimized execution.
review_notes.claude-compatible: Best risk-adjusted strategy in the portfolio. Requires zero custom CUDA code, so compile risk is eliminated entirely. torch.compile with reduce-overhead and static shapes enables CUDA graph replay across the 13-block MBConv sequential, directly attacking the Python dispatch overhead that structured benchmarks expose. The caveats (warm-up cost, fullgraph breaks on conditional residual) are real but addressable by falling back to fullgraph=False. Highest usefulness-to-risk ratio given the EfficientNetB0 architecture.
review_notes.gemini-compatible: Using torch.compile with reduce-overhead is a very high-leverage strategy that can automatically fuse operations and eliminate Python dispatch overhead via CUDA graphs.

Use vectorized loads (float4) where the spatial dimension is large enough (stem: 32 channels over 112x112; head: 1280 channels over 7x7) to maximize memory throughput.
Export two entrypoints from cuda_cpp: bn_relu_stem and bn_relu_head, each taking the conv output tensor plus precomputed scale/shift tensors.
In init_body, register buffers for fused_scale_stem, fused_shift_stem, fused_scale_head, fused_shift_head and populate them in a post-init hook or lazily on first forward when eval.
Keep the standard fallback path for training mode since running stats are updated during training.

risk_notes: Must detect eval vs train mode and fall back to standard nn.BatchNorm2d path during training to preserve running statistics updates.
